text: @sleetdrop/dsh-plugin-topology 是面向 DSH Web 客户端的插件依赖拓扑检查器。它通过 Cordis 服务读取运行中的插件与服务关系，提供模型可调用的 graph_render 工具和侧边栏全局页面。可以查看插件及服务节点、依赖边、未解析依赖和图指标，搜索插件或服务并检查邻接关系，还能将结果导出为 JSON、Graphviz DOT 或 SVG。适合排查 DSH 运行时插件装配关系、理解服务依赖并分享拓扑图的开发者。源码没有要求 API 密钥或外部账户。

@sleetdrop/dsh-plugin-topology maps DSH plugin and service dependencies. Its host service powers a model tool and web page to inspect graph metrics and unresolved services, explore node relationships, and export JSON, DOT, or SVG. It helps developers trace runtime plugin assembly.
想看清 DSH 里各个插件依赖了哪些服务。
能不能把运行中的插件依赖关系画成图？
帮我找出哪些插件声明了没有提供者的服务。
我想搜索某个插件或服务，再查看它连接的对象。
How can I inspect which DSH plugins depend on a particular service?
I need an exportable dependency graph of the plugins running in DSH.
@sleetdrop/dsh-plugin-topology 的功能「拓扑分析」：服务快照记录插件、服务及注入关系，并计算依赖图和图指标；调用 analyze 获取结果。
@sleetdrop/dsh-plugin-topology 的功能「图形导出」：调用 graph_render 选择 JSON、DOT 或 SVG，生成依赖图文档；网页也可下载这些格式。
@sleetdrop/dsh-plugin-topology 的功能「交互式检查」：侧栏页面支持搜索插件或服务、查看依赖邻居与未解析服务，并展示图指标。

@sleetdrop/dsh-plugin-topology README · @sleetdrop/dsh-plugin-topology：[](https://github.com/sleetdrop/dsh-plugin-topology/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

Plugin dependency graph inspector for DeepSeek Harness. It snapshots the live
Cordis plugin fiber tree into a plugin/service bipartite graph, derives
graph-theory metrics, and renders it as JSON, Graphviz DOT, or SVG.

One installable bundle ships three surfaces:

@sleetdrop/dsh-plugin-topology README · @sleetdrop/dsh-plugin-topology：- **host service** (`@sleetdrop/dsh-plugin-topology`): a `TypertRemoteService`
  exposing `analyze()` and `render()` over the gateway.
- **host tool** (`@sleetdrop/dsh-plugin-topology/tool`): the model-facing
  `graph_render` tool, registering on `ctx.tools`.
- **browser surface** (`dsh.client`): a global page reachable from the sidebar's
  panel list that renders the graph, metrics, legend, unresolved-dependency log,
  and pan/zoom + format downloads.
@sleetdrop/dsh-plugin-topology README · Install：```sh
@sleetdrop/dsh-plugin-topology README · From the npm registry (prebuilt lib/, no build permission needed):：dsh plugin --profile <name> add @sleetdrop/dsh-plugin-topology

The bundle patch mounts the host service row and the `graph_render` tool row.
The tool row can live in the profile patch instead — a deployment that prefers
per-session placement may remove it from `cordis.patch.yml` and add it to its
agent preset.

@sleetdrop/dsh-plugin-topology README · Model Experience：The `graph_render` tool serializes the running instance's plugin dependency
graph as one document:

@sleetdrop/dsh-plugin-topology README · Model Experience：- `json` — a NetworkX-compatible node-link graph whose nodes carry graph-theory
  metrics (in/out degree, degree/betweenness/eigenvector centrality, page-rank)
  and whose `graph` object carries global metrics (density, strongly connected
  components, `isDag`, diameter).
- `dot` — Graphviz source for layout via any Graphviz tool.
- `svg` — a Graphviz-rendered SVG, with isolated plugins composed beside the
  main graph.

@sleetdrop/dsh-plugin-topology README · Model Experience：For `dot` or `svg`, write the returned content to a file with the write tool to
produce a shareable artifact. Use `json` to inspect or analyze the assembly.

@sleetdrop/dsh-plugin-topology README · Screenshots：The page renders the live plugin/service topology as a zoomable Graphviz
graph, with metrics, a color legend, and an unresolved-dependency table. The
same view is localized through the harness locale dictionaries:

- [Chinese (zh_CN)](docs/screenshots/panel-zh_CN.png)
- [English (en_US)](docs/screenshots/panel-en_US.png)

@sleetdrop/dsh-plugin-topology README · Browser page：The entry is a global-panel row in the sidebar (`sidebar.panellist`), visible
with or without a selected session — the topology is runtime-global and needs
no session context. The row addresses the `main` panel keyed `plugin-topology`,
so the view occupies the center column under the harness's page chrome (on
macOS it clears the window's traffic-light strip); leaving it is ordinary
sidebar navigation, exactly like the Plugins page, with no window controls of
its own. Same-named plugin instances merge into one node; each node's label
carries the instance creation ordinals in brackets (`timer[1,9,23]`), assigned
at startup and meaningful only within that run.

@sleetdrop/dsh-plugin-topology README · Node inspection：The SVG renders inline, so the graph is interactive without baking anything
into the export — a downloaded SVG still opens clean in any viewer.

@sleetdrop/dsh-plugin-topology README · Node inspection：- **Hover** raises a light ring on the node, nothing else.
- **Click** selects the node and opens a fixed inspector on the right (360px
  with a selection, 300px as an empty hint rail, collapsible to 40px). It shows
  the fiber `state`, module `source`, and two independently scrolling sections:
  `→ Dependencies` and `← Dependents`.
  Each row carries a state dot, the instance ordinals, and the mediating
  service(s); clicking a row selects and flies to that target.
- **The inspector header** links the name to npm and carries `Frame all` per
  direction, collapse, and close. A local filter narrows both sections by name
  or service and shows `matching / total`; it never changes the graph
  highlight. Section heights follow their row counts, so one direction cannot
  push the other out of view.
- **Breadcrumb + history**: the canvas keeps the visited path (`… / current`)
  at the top left. There is no leading "Overview" crumb: fitting the whole graph
  belongs to the zoom control, and a mode switch inside a path read like a
  reset. `←`, `Backspace` or `⌘[` returns to the previous selection; the
  breadcrumb segments are clicka

@sleetdrop/dsh-plugin-topology README · Node inspection：Degree counts are read from the rendered SVG rather than the raw snapshot, so a
merged node reports the edges actually drawn after the projection collapses
same-named instances.

The client injects `remote` (the gateway ClientRemote service) and self-mounts
its own `pluginTopology` Remote contribution, so it does not require editing
the host assembly's contribution list.

@sleetdrop/dsh-plugin-topology README · Compatibility：The plugin uses its **own independent semantic version** — it does not mirror
the DeepSeek Harness version. New plugin features and bugfixes bump the plugin
version on their own schedule, independent of which DSH release it targets.
The table below maps each plugin version to the DSH release it was validated
against, so pick the plugin version whose target DSH matches your harness.

@sleetdrop/dsh-plugin-topology README · Compatibility：Current release targets DeepSeek Harness `0.2.2-rc.1`; the `peerDependencies`
pin the client packages and `@deepseek-ai/cordis@^4.1.0` the snapshot reads
through. The 0.1.2 rc line removed the old `dsh-client-runtime` browser runtime:
the client now runs on the Cordis `Context` augmented by the shell baseline
renderer (`dsh-client-ui-renderer` → `ctx.slots`), `dsh-client-store`
(`defineStore`), `dsh-client-locale` (`ctx.locale`), and `dsh-api-remotes`
(`ctx.remote`). The service reads Cordis internals (`root.registry`,
`root.reflect.store`, fiber fields) to observe the assembly itself — those
surfaces are deliberately not part of the stable public API, so pick a plugin
version whose target DSH matches your harness, and verify the installed harness
satisfies the peer ranges before enabling the tool or page.

@sleetdrop/dsh-plugin-topology README · Compatibility：DSH itself has no beta channel — it publishes `alpha` then `rc`. Follow its
`next` dist-tag: `latest` is not a dependable pointer across the suite, because
the individual `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` packages leave it on an older prerelease
rather than moving it with `next`. This plugin adapts to stable DSH `rc`
releases only and skips the fast-moving `alpha` line.

@sleetdrop/dsh-plugin-topology README · Known Limitations：- This plugin deliberately reads Cordis internals (`root.registry`,
  `root.reflect.store`, fiber fields) to observe the live assembly itself —
  that is the point of the project, and those internal surfaces are not part of
  Cordis's stable public API. A future Cordis that reshapes them breaks
  `snapshot()` and we follow the installed Cordis version with each upgrade
  rather than shimming around it; the breakage surfaces as a bare type error and
  the field mapping is logged in `docs/DSH-UPGRADE.md`.
- The browser page requires a web profile (the `--patch` overlay covers only
  the node half).
- Same-named instances merge in the display graph; per-instance identity stays
  available in the JSON export and the complete downloadable DOT.

@sleetdrop/dsh-plugin-topology README · Development：```sh
pnpm install
pnpm check   # CI-equivalent: typecheck, build, tests, drift, pack, compat
```

`pnpm check` includes the deterministic drift checks (orphaned `lib/`, client
externals, DSH theme tokens, package payload, README/RELEASING/peer
compatibility) and the locale/inspector model tests; CI runs the same matrix on
Node 22 and 24.

@sleetdrop/dsh-plugin-topology README · Development：The `dsh.client` browser bundle inlines everything except the shell's frozen
platform-module rows it requires (`react`, `react/jsx-runtime`,
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-store`, and `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-primitives`),
which every supported harness shell serves. `scripts/check-client-externals.mjs`
fails `pnpm check` if the bundle requires anything else.

@sleetdrop/dsh-plugin-topology README · Development：See [NEXT-STEPS.md](NEXT-STEPS.md) for planned renderer improvements and
[docs/QUALITY.md](https://github.com/sleetdrop/dsh-plugin-topology/blob/main/docs/QUALITY.md) for the quality/drift workstream.

@sleetdrop/dsh-plugin-topology README · Publishing：The full end-to-end release checklist (version bump → build/test → commit/tag →
headless + browser smoke → publish) is in [`docs/RELEASING.md`](docs/RELEASING.md).
The final publish requires an interactive OTP, so it is run by hand. A portable
helper script handles the registry/login guards, publish, and verification:

```sh
./scripts/publish.sh   # prompts for login (if needed) and OTP
```

@sleetdrop/dsh-plugin-topology README · Publishing：`prepublishOnly` runs `pnpm check` (the CI-equivalent gate). `publishConfig` pins `access:
public` and the `registry.npmjs.org` target. If `npm publish` fails with an
`EPERM` from the npm cache (`root-owned files`), either fix the cache once
(`sudo chown -R $(id -u):$(id -g) ~/.npm`) or publish through pnpm, whose
store avoids the npm cache entirely:

```sh
pnpm publish                    # same prepublishOnly gate, pnpm store
```

@sleetdrop/dsh-plugin-topology README · Publishing：`files` ships `lib/`, `cordis.patch.yml`, `overlay.example.yml`, and
`NEXT-STEPS.md`; npm adds README and LICENSE automatically.
